To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the general population shows sex differences in empathizing and systemising, (ii) people on the autistic spectrum are characterized by empathizing deficits and hypersystemizing, (iii) hypersystemizing can explain the preference for systems characterized by highly lawful change in people with ASC, (iv) hypersystemizing is a strong drive to discover the "Truth", and (v) the Truth is defined as lawful regularities or patterns in data, including patterns in change.
people with ASC are driven by a strong need to discover the "true" patterns in data, and that this need is so strong that it can be disabling when the data are complex.

Autistic spectrum conditions are characterized by an unusual drive to systemize that can be explained by the hypersystemizing hypothesis, which proposes that people with autism spectrum conditions are strongly driven to find the "truth", defined as patterns in data that change in highly predictable ways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between autism, systemizing, and truth.
the relationship between truth, empathy, and systemizing.
the question of whether truth is a universal value.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hypersystemizing hypothesis is a promising theory that explains a number of features of ASC, but it does not yet provide a complete explanation of ASC.
the hypersystemizing drive is a necessary but not a sufficient cause of autism spectrum conditions.
, in general, women are more empathic than men, and that men are more likely than women to be hypersystemizers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the autistic mind, "truth" is a systemizing construct.
the hypersystemizing drive in ASC is a drive to find truth.
people with ASC are truth seekers, who are disabled when the world fails to be true.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, people on the autistic spectrum are hypersystemizers and that this is a major factor in their difficulties.
, for people with ASC, truth may be defined differently from the rest of the population, and that this may have important implications in the classroom, in the workplace, and in society.
the hypersystemizing account of ASC is consistent with a strong truth-seeking drive in people with ASC.
